newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed mixed amid confusion over USDA's estimate for Brazil. January gave up $6.00 to close at $1,290 per tonne while March added $11 to close at $1,243. Fears over a frost in Mexico's coffee areas appear to have abated. In New York arabica futures moved up sharply after starting off the session on a slower note. Fuelling the rise was a USDA Attache report which seemed to be a downward revision of the Brazilian production estimate released a week ago. The USDA Attache in Sao Paulo pegged Brazil's 1996/97 crop at 25.8 million 60-kg bags, down from 27 million bags put forth a week ago. What traders found curious was that the report was dated in seemingly ample time for the USDA to have reflected the change in the world production estimate released last week, but opted not to.

Later the market staged a quick retreat when a USDA crops analyst reiterated the Department's 27.0 million bag-forecast, explaining that the Attache's report, now seven weeks old, had since been revised. USDA's specialty crop's analyst Edmond Missiaen said there were no plans to revised the 27.0 million bag-estimate put forth recently until next June. March finished 1.95 cents/lb higher at 112.15 cents/lb, while May added 2.15 cents/lb to close at 109.60 cents/lb. The outer months added 1.65 to 2.30 cents/lb.

BRAZIL - The USDA Attache in Brazil reduced the estimate of Brazil's coffee production for the 1996/97 marketing year (July/June) by 6 percent to 25.8 million 60-kg bags. According to an Attache report dated November 5 but released on December 20, the forecast of coffee exports for 1996/97 is 16.5 million bags, based on a decrease in the total Brazilian production estimate and the resulting decrease in exportable supplies. The new forecast is down 9 percent from the previous forecast. The Attache reduced the estimate of the country's production mainly because of a reduction in output in central/west Brazil. Earlier, estimates were too high, the report said. Also, a recent tour of the area showed that production was not as large as expected. The export estimate includes 14 million bags of green coffee and 2.5 million bags of soluble exports, the report said.

TAIWAN - Taiwan imported 17,165 bags of coffee in September 1996, down from 18,550 bags imported the previous month. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 to 156,239 bags. The county imports most of its coffee in the form of solubles. Main suppliers of solubles in January/September 1996 were South Korea (31,200 bags), Malaysia (10,100 bags) and Singapore (15,900 bags). However, the country not only imports but also exports solubles. Soluble exports in January/September 1996 were 70,000 bags, of which 24,000 bags were exported to the United States, 12,600 bags to the Netherlands and 12,700 bags to Brunei.

TANZANIA - Tanzania exported 152,500 bags of coffee in July/October 1996, 16 percent less than in the same period in 1995. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (October/July) reached 934,800 bags, sharply up from the 611,900 bags exported in 1994/95. Main countries of destination for green coffee were Germany (333,600 bags), the Netherlands (109,300 bags) and Japan (188,700 bags).
